headings: The Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation Improvement Act
paragraphs: Blue Ridge Bankshares, Inc. (the "Company") is a bank holding company headquartered in Richmond, Virginia. The Company provides commercial and consumer banking and financial services through its wholly-owned bank subsidiary, Blue Ridge Bank, National Association (the "Bank"), and its wealth and trust management subsidiary, BRB Financial Group, Inc. (the "Financial Group"). The Company was incorporated under the laws of the Commonwealth of Virginia in July 1988.

The Bank is a federally chartered national bank with its main office in Martinsville, Virginia that traces its roots to Page Valley Bank of Virginia, which opened for business in 1893. At December 31, 2025, the Bank operated twenty-seven full-service banking offices across its footprint, which stretches from the Shenandoah Valley across the Piedmont region through Richmond and into the coastal peninsulas and the Hampton Roads region of Virginia and into central North Carolina.

The Bank serves businesses, professionals, consumers, nonprofits, and municipalities with a wide variety of financial services, including retail and commercial banking. Banking products include checking accounts, savings accounts, money market accounts, cash management accounts, certificates of deposit, individual retirement accounts, commercial and industrial loans, residential mortgages, commercial mortgages, home equity loans, consumer installment loans, credit cards, online banking, telephone banking, and mobile banking. Deposits of the Bank are insured by the Deposit Insurance Fund (the "DIF") of the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (the "FDIC") to the full extent of the limits of the DIF.

The Company, through the Financial Group, offers investment and wealth management and management services for personal and corporate trusts, including estate planning, estate settlement, trust administration, and life insurance products. The Company, through its minority investment in Hammond Insurance Agency, Incorporated, offers property and casualty insurance to individuals and businesses.

The Company's primary source of revenue is interest income from its lending activities. The Company's other sources of revenue are interest and dividend income from investments, interest income from its interest-earning deposit balances in other depository institutions, transactions and fee income from its lending and deposit activities, and income associated with wealth and trust management services. The Company's major expenses are interest on deposits and general and administrative expenses, such as employee salaries and benefits, FDIC assessments, data processing expenses, technology costs, and professional services expenses.

The Company historically had partnerships with financial technology ("fintech") providers, through which it provided indirect depository services (referred to as banking-as-a-service or "BaaS") to both consumers and businesses. Fintech companies provided technologies to enable the delivery of digital bank services and were a source of interest and fee income, and deposits. During 2024, the Company, through an orderly wind down, exited its BaaS depository operations; therefore, as of December 31, 2025, the Company had no active end-users attained through fintech channels. The Company provides indirect lending services through fintech partnerships. In these arrangements, the fintech partner sources the loans, which the Bank then originates. The loans are then purchased by the fintech partner or other third-party generally up to three days from origination. As of December 31, 2025, the Company offered indirect fintech lending services conducted through Upgrade, Inc. As of December 31, 2024, the Company offered indirect fintech lending services conducted through Upgrade, Inc., Best Egg, Inc., Kashable, LLC, and Grow Credit, Inc. The Company has been terminating its indirect fintech lending relationships and expects to be completely exited in 2026.

As of December 31, 2025, the Company had total assets of approximately $2.43 billion, total gross loans of approximately $1.87 billion, total deposits of approximately $1.91 billion, and stockholders' equity of approximately $323.7 million.

During much of 2025, the Bank was subject to a Consent Order (the "Consent Order") issued on January 24, 2024 by its primary regulator, the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (the "OCC"). The Consent Order primarily concerned the Bank's fintech operations and required the Bank to continue enhancing its controls for assessing and managing risks stemming from its fintech partnerships and added time frames for meeting certain of the directives, required the Bank to submit a strategic plan and a capital plan, and required the Bank to maintain a leverage ratio of 10.0% and a total capital ratio
of 13.0%, referred to as minimum capital ratios. On November 13, 2025, the OCC issued an order terminating the Consent Order effective the same date.
Complete copies of the Consent Order and the Order Terminating the Consent Order issued by the OCC are included as Exhibits 10.9 and 99.1, respectively, to this Annual Report on Form 10-K.

On October 27, 2025, the Company announced a special cash dividend of $0.25 per share of the Company's common stock totaling approximately $29.1 million. Of this amount, $22.6 million was paid on November 21, 2025, to shareholders of record as of the close of business on November 7, 2025. The remaining $6.5 million was established as a liability and will be paid if and when warrants to purchase common stock are exercised and if and when performance-based restricted stock awards ("PSAs") vest (collectively, the "Special Cash Dividend").

On August 25, 2025, the Company announced the adoption of a share repurchase program (the "Repurchase Program") pursuant to which the Company may purchase up to $15.0 million of the Company's common stock.

Repurchases may be made in open market purchases, block trades, or privately negotiated transactions, including upon the exercise of outstanding warrants to purchase common stock. The Company cannot predict when or if it will repurchase additional shares of common stock as the Repurchase Program will depend on a number of factors, including constraints specified in any Securities and Exchange Commission Rule 10b5-1 trading plans, price, and general business and market conditions.

For the year ended December 31, 2025, the Company repurchased 802,735 shares of its common stock at a weighted average price of $4.17 per share totaling $3.4 million. Additionally, the Company repurchased outstanding warrants to purchase 3,229,000 shares of its common stock at a weighted average price of $1.90 per warrant totaling $6.1 million. For additional information regarding the Repurchase Program, see Part II, Item 5 of this Form 10-K.

paragraphs: An investment in the Company's common stock involves certain risks, including those described below. In addition to the other information set forth in this Form 10-K, investors in the Company's securities should carefully consider the factors discussed below. These factors, either alone or taken together, could materially and adversely affect the Company's business, financial condition, liquidity, results of operations, capital position, and prospects. One or more of these could cause the Company's actual results to differ materially from its historical results or the results contemplated by the forward-looking statements contained in this report, in which case the trading price of the Company's securities could decline.

A key aspect of the Company's long-term business strategy is growth. During 2025 and 2024, the Company's strategic initiatives included repositioning its balance sheet to align with its return to a community-focused bank and positioning itself for measured growth. The Company may not be able to successfully grow in the long-term if it is unable to identify attractive markets, locations, or opportunities to expand in the future. The Company's ability to manage its growth successfully also will depend on whether it can maintain capital levels adequate to support its business, maintain operational and control systems, cost controls, asset quality, comply with regulatory requirements, and successfully integrate any businesses the Company pursues into its organization.

Should the Company enter into new markets or new lines of business, its lack of history and familiarity with those markets, clients, and lines of business may lead to unexpected challenges or difficulties that inhibit its success. The Company's plans to expand could depress earnings in the short run, even if it efficiently executes a growth strategy leading to long-term financial benefits. Any of the foregoing could adversely affect the Company's results of operations.

The Company has reported net income for the year ended December 31, 2025, but reported a net loss for the year ended December 31, 2024, some of which is due to the cost of complying with regulatory directives set forth in the Consent Order. While the Company has implemented, and will continue to implement, cost-saving initiatives and efficiency measures, there is no guarantee that these actions will yield the desired financial results. Additionally, the Company reduced its earning assets in 2025 and 2024 and intends to begin increasing earning assets in future periods. Factors such as market conditions, competitive pressures, or unforeseen operational challenges could hinder the Company's ability to achieve sustained and acceptable levels of future profitability. If the Company is unable to improve its financial performance, it could experience less than acceptable levels of profits, which could adversely affect its financial position, capital levels, and the value of its common stock.

The Company's success is, and is expected to remain, highly dependent on its management team. The Company's strategy and operations will continue to place significant demands on management, and the loss of any such person's services may have an adverse effect upon the Company's strategy, operations, and profitability. If the Company fails to retain or continue to recruit qualified employees, its strategy, operations, and profitability could be adversely affected.

In order to be successful, the Company must identify and retain experienced key management members and sales staff with local expertise and relationships. Competition for qualified personnel is intense and there is a limited number of qualified persons with knowledge of and experience in banking and in the Company's chosen geographic markets. Even if the Company identifies individuals that it believes could assist it in building its franchise, it may be unable to recruit these individuals to work for the Company. In addition, the process of identifying and recruiting individuals with the combination of skills and attributes required to carry out the Company's strategy is often lengthy. The Company's inability to identify, recruit, and retain talented personnel could limit its ability to pursue its strategic goals and materially adversely affect its business, financial condition, and results of operations.

paragraphs: The following presents management's discussion and analysis of the Company's consolidated financial condition and the results of the Company's operations. This discussion should be read in conjunction with the Company's consolidated financial statements and the notes thereto presented in Item 8, Financial Statements and Supplementary Information, of this Form 10-K.

The Company makes certain forward-looking statements in this Form 10-K that are subject to risks and uncertainties. These forward-looking statements represent plans, estimates, objectives, goals, guidelines, expectations, intentions, projections, and statements of management's beliefs concerning future events, business plans, objectives, expected operating results, and the assumptions upon which those statements are based. Forward-looking statements include without limitation, any statement that may predict, forecast, indicate, or imply future results, performance or achievements, and are typically identified with words such as "may," "could," "should," "will," "would," "believe," "anticipate," "estimate," "expect," "aim," "intend," "plan," or words of similar meaning. The Company cautions that the forward-looking statements are based largely on management's expectations and are subject to a number of known and unknown risks and uncertainties that may change based on factors which are, in many instances, beyond its control. Actual results, performance, or achievements could differ materially from those contemplated, expressed, or implied by the forward-looking statements.
The following factors, among others, could cause the Company's financial performance to differ materially from that expressed in such forward-looking statements:
• the strength of the United States economy in general and the strength of the local economies in which the Company conducts operations;
• the effects of, and changes in, the macroeconomic environment and financial market conditions, including monetary and fiscal policies, interest rates, and inflation;
• reputational risk and potential adverse reactions of the Company's customers, suppliers, employees, or other business partners;
• the quality and composition of the Company's loan and investment portfolios, including changes in the level of the Company's nonperforming assets and charge-offs;

• the Company's management of risks inherent in its loan portfolio, the credit quality of its borrowers, and the risk of a prolonged downturn in the real estate market, which could impair the value of the Company's collateral and its ability to sell collateral upon any foreclosure;
• the ability to maintain adequate liquidity by growing and retaining deposits and secondary funding sources, especially if the Company's or its industry's reputation become damaged;

• the emergence of digital assets and payment stablecoins, and evolving legislative or regulatory frameworks, which could alter deposit flows, competition, and credit intermediation and, in turn, adversely affect the Company's funding, liquidity, or overall financial performance;
• the ability to maintain capital levels adequate to support the Company's business;
• the ability of the Company to implement cost-saving initiatives and efficiency measures, as well as increase earning assets, in order to yield acceptable levels of profitability;
• the ability to generate sufficient future taxable income for the Company to realize its deferred tax assets, including the net operating loss carryforward;

• the usage of advances and changes in technological and social media to develop timely and competitive products and services, and the acceptance of these products and services by new and existing customers;

paragraphs: Blue Ridge Bankshares, Inc. (the "Company") 為一間總部設於維吉尼亞州里奇蒙的銀行控股公司。本公司透過其百分之百擁有之銀行子公司 Blue Ridge Bank, National Association (the "Bank")，以及其財富與信託管理子公司 BRB Financial Group, Inc. (the "Financial Group")，提供商業與消費者銀行及金融服務。本公司於 1988 年 7 月根據維吉尼亞州法律設立。
Bank 為一間根據美國聯邦法律設立的國家銀行，總部設於維吉尼亞州馬丁斯維爾，其歷史可追溯至 1893 年開業的維吉尼亞州 Page Valley Bank。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，Bank 在其服務範圍內經營了 27 間全功能銀行分行，服務範圍從雪倫多亞谷地經皮德蒙特地區，穿越里奇蒙，延伸至維吉尼亞州海岸半島及漢普頓羅茲地區，並進入北卡羅萊納州中部。

Bank 提供多樣化的金融服務，服務對象包括企業、專業人士、消費者、非營利組織及地方政府，包括零售與商業銀行服務。銀行產品包括支票帳戶、儲蓄帳戶、貨幣市場帳戶、現金管理帳戶、定期存款、個人退休帳戶、商業與工業貸款、住宅抵押貸款、商業抵押貸款、住宅貸款、消費者分期貸款、信用卡、網際網路銀行、電話銀行及行動銀行。Bank 的存款由美國聯邦存款保險公司 (the "FDIC") 的存款保險基金 (the "DIF") 保險，保險範圍至 DIF 的最高限額。
本公司透過 Financial Group 提供投資與財富管理及管理服務，服務個人與企業信託，包括遺產規劃、遺產處理、信託管理及人壽保險產品。本公司透過其在 Hammond Insurance Agency, Incorporated 的少數投資，提供財產與意外保險給個人與企業。
本公司的主要收入來源為貸款活動產生的利息收入。本公司的其他收入來源包括投資產生的利息與股息收入、在其他存款機構的存款產生的利息收入、貸款與存款活動產生的交易與費用收入，以及與財富與信託管理服務相關的收入。本公司的主要費用為存款利息及一般與行政費用，例如員工薪資與福利、FDIC 保險費、資料處理費用、資訊科技費用及專業服務費用。

本公司歷來與金融科技 ("fintech") 提供商有合作關係，透過這些合作關係，本公司為消費者與企業提供間接存款服務 (稱為銀行即服務或 "BaaS")。Fintech 公司提供技術以實現數位銀行服務，並為本公司帶來利息與費用收入，以及存款。在 2024 年，本公司透過有序收縮，退出其 BaaS 存款業務；因此，截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，本公司透過 fintech 頻道未有活躍的最終用戶。本公司透過 fintech 合作關係提供間接貸款服務。在這些安排中，fintech 合作夥伴會取得貸款，由 Bank 原始發放。貸款在發放後最多三日內由 fintech 合作夥伴或其他第三方購入。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，本公司透過 Upgrade, Inc. 提供間接 fintech 貸款服務。截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日，本公司透過 Upgrade, Inc., Best Egg, Inc., Kashable, LLC，以及 Grow Credit, Inc. 提供間接 fintech 貸款服務。本公司正在終止其間接 fintech 貸款關係，預期於 2026 年完全退出。
截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，本公司總資產約為 2.43 十億美元，總貸款約為 1.87 十億美元，總存款約為 1.91 十億美元，以及股東權益約為 323.7 百萬美元。

在 2025 年的大部分時間，Bank 受到一項同意令 (the "Consent Order") 的限制，該同意令於 2024 年 1 月 24 日由其主要監管機構美國國庫局 (the "OCC") 發出。該同意令主要涉及 Bank 的 fintech 業務，要求 Bank 繼續強化其風險評估與管理控制，以應對其 fintech 合作夥伴帶來的風險，並延長達成某些指令的時間，要求 Bank 提交戰略計畫與資本計畫，並要求 Bank 保持 10.0% 的槓桿比率與總資本比率
13.0% 之比率，稱為最低資本比率。2025 年 11 月 13 日，OCC 發佈命令終止 Consent Order，該命令自同日生效。
Consent Order 及由 OCC 發佈之終止 Consent Order 之完整副本，分別作為本 10-K 年度報告之附錄 10.9 與 99.1 處列示。
2025 年 10 月 27 日，本公司宣佈發放特別現金紅利，每股 0.25 美元，總計約 29.1 百萬美元。此金額中，22.6 百萬美元於 2025 年 11 月 21 日支付給 2025 年 11 月 7 日營業結束時登記為本公司普通股股東之股東。剩餘 6.5 百萬美元已列為負債，將在行使購買普通股之權證及績效基準限制性股票獎勵（"PSAs"）解禁時（合稱 "特別現金紅利"）支付。
2025 年 8 月 25 日，本公司宣佈採用一股股份回購計畫（"Repurchase Program"），根據此計畫，本公司可購買最多 15.0 百萬美元之本公司普通股。
回購可透過公開市場買賣、大宗交易或私下協議進行，包括行使現有購買普通股之權證。本公司無法預測是否或何時會回購更多普通股，因 Repurchase Program 會視多種因素而定，包括任何證券交易委員會 Rule 10b5-1 交易計畫所規定之限制、價格及總體經濟與市場條件。
截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日之會計年度，本公司回購其普通股 802,735 股，加權平均價格為每股 4.17 美元，總計 3.4 百萬美元。此外，本公司亦回購現有購買 3,229,000 股普通股之權證，加權平均價格為每權證 1.90 美元，總計 6.1 百萬美元。有關 Repurchase Program 之更多資訊，請參閱本 10-K 表單之第二部分，第 5 項。

paragraphs: 以下為管理階層對本公司整體財務狀況及營運成果之討論與分析。請配合本公司整體財務報表及相關附註，一併閱讀本表 10-K 第 8 項「財務報表與補充資料」之內容。

本公司於本表 10-K 中提出若干展望性陳述，這些陳述受風險與不確定性所影響。這些展望性陳述包含計畫、預估、目標、指引、期望、意圖、預測及管理階層對未來事件、營運計畫、目標、預期營運成果及相關陳述所依據之假設的信念。展望性陳述包含但不限於任何預測、預測、表示或暗示未來結果、表現或成就之陳述，通常會以「可能」、「或許」、「應該」、「將」、「會」、「相信」、「預期」、「估計」、「期望」、「目標」、「意圖」、「計畫」或相似意義之詞彙來識別。本公司提醒，這些展望性陳述主要基於管理階層之預期，並受許多已知及未知之風險與不確定性影響，這些風險與不確定性可能因許多因素而改變，而這些因素在許多情況下皆超出本公司之控制範圍。實際結果、表現或成就可能與展望性陳述所預期、表達或暗示者有重大差異。
以下因素，及其他因素，可能導致本公司財務表現與展望性陳述所表達者有重大差異：
• 美國整體經濟強弱，以及本公司營運所在地區之地方經濟強弱；
• 總體經濟環境與金融市場條件的影響及變化，包括貨幣與財政政策、利率及通貨膨脹；
• 本公司之聲譽風險及潛在的客戶、供應商、員工或其他商業夥伴之不利反應；
• 本公司貸款與投資組合之品質與組成，包括本公司非放款資產與核銷金額之水準變化；
• 本公司管理貸款組合內固有風險、借款人之信用品質及實體不景氣持續時間風險，此等風險可能影響本公司擔保品價值及其在任何拍賣時出售擔保品之能力。
• 本公司能否維持足夠的流動性，透過擴張並保留存款及次要資金來源，特別是在本公司或其產業聲譽受損的情況下;
• 數位資產與穩定幣的出現，以及演變中的立法或監管架構，可能改變存款流向、競爭情形與信用中介，進而對本公司的資金、流動性或整體財務表現產生不利影響;
• 本公司能否維持足夠的資本水平，以支撐本公司業務;
• 本公司能否實施節省成本的措施與提高效率，以及增加獲利資產，以達到可接受的獲利水準;
• 本公司能否產生足夠的未來應稅所得，以實現其遞延所得稅資產，包括淨營業虧損結轉;
• 利用先進技術與科技及社會媒體，以發展及時且具競爭力的產品與服務，以及這些產品與服務被新舊客戶接受的情形;

headings: 本公司可能無法成功管理其成長，這可能會對其營運成果及財務狀況造成不利影響。
本公司可能無法在未來產生可接受程度的獲利水平。
本公司之成功取決於其管理團隊，任何這些人員的意外流失可能會對營運造成不利影響。
本公司策略的成功取決於其識別並留住具市場經驗及人脈之個體的能力。
本公司業務面臨利率風險，以及利率變動，若無法妥善管理利率風險，可能會對財務表現產生負面影響。
經濟條件的變化，特別是在本公司營運地區，可能會對其業務產生重大且負面的影響。
本公司可能因市場條件變動而受到不利影響。
本公司業務及盈餘受政府、財政及貨幣政策影響，而本公司對這些政策毫無控制權。
本公司面臨來自金融服務公司及其他提供銀行及其它金融服務公司的強勁且持續成長的競爭，這可能會對本公司業務產生負面影響。
消費者可能越來越傾向不使用銀行來完成其金融交易，這將對本公司財務狀況及營運產生重大不利影響。
本公司普通股流動性不足，且可能不會發展出更活躍的普通股交易市場，這可能會限制股東出售其股份的能力，並可能增加價格波動性。
本公司信用標準及其持續信用評估程序可能無法保護本公司免於重大信用損失。
本公司信用損失準備金（"ACL"）可能不足，任何信用損失準備金的增加都可能對本公司財務狀況及營運成果產生重大不利影響。
不良資產需要長時間才能解決，且會對本公司營運成果及財務狀況產生不利影響。
本公司對以不動產為擔保的貸款之集中度，可能增加其未來信用損失，此將對本公司之財務結果產生負面影響。
本公司對商業不動產之信用風險敞口具有中度集中度，且以此類擔保品為抵押之貸款被視為具有較高違約風險。
本公司對中小型社區企業之貸款重點，可能增加其信用風險。
本公司之營運結果受借款人償還貸款能力之影響極大。
本公司依賴客戶及交易對手之資訊之準確性與完整性，若本公司依賴錯誤或不正確資訊，將可能對本公司財務狀況產生負面影響。
本公司對其取得所有權之不動產可能面臨環境責任之風險。
本公司之營運可能因網路安全風險而受到負面影響。
本公司依賴其他公司提供其業務基礎建設之關鍵零組件。
會計準則之變更可能影響報告之營業收入。
未能維持有效之內部及揭露控製系統，可能對本公司之營運結果及財務狀況產生重大不利影響。
其他金融機構之健全性可能對本公司產生不利影響。
本公司面臨多種營運風險，包括聲譽風險、法律風險及合規風險，以及員工、董事或外部人士詐欺或竊取之風險。
本公司能否獲利營運，可能取決於其能否將各種技術整合或引入營運中。
人工智慧（"AI"）之發展與應用，可能對本公司業務產生風險與挑戰。
paragraphs: 投資本公司普通股涉及某些風險，包括下列所描述的風險。除本 Form 10-K 所載的其他資訊外，投資本公司證券的投資人應謹慎考量下列所討論的各項因素。這些因素，無論單獨或共同作用，都可能對本公司業務、財務狀況、流動性、營運成果、資本狀況與前景產生重大且不利的影響。其中一項或多項因素可能導致本公司實際結果與歷史結果或本報告所包含的預測性陳述所預期的結果有重大差異，屆時本公司證券的交易價格可能下跌。

本公司長期業務策略的一個關鍵方面是成長。在 2025 年及 2024 年，本公司戰略重點包括重新定位資產負債表以符合其重返社區導向銀行的目標，並為可衡量的成長做準備。若本公司無法識別具吸引力的市場、地點或未來擴張的機會，則可能無法在長遠內成功成長。本公司能否成功管理其成長，也將取決於其是否能維持足夠的資本水平以支撐其業務、維持運營與控制系統、成本控制、資產品質、符合監管要求，並成功整合任何本公司追求的業務至其組織中。
若本公司進入新市場或新業務線，其缺乏這些市場、客戶與業務線的歷史與熟悉度，可能導致未預期的挑戰或困難，進而影響其成功。本公司擴張計畫可能在短期內壓低獲利，即使其能有效執行成長策略以帶來長期財務效益。上述任何情況都可能對本公司營運成果產生不利影響。

本公司於 2025 年 12 月 31 日財年報告淨收入，但於 2024 年 12 月 31 日財年報告淨虧損，部分原因係因遵守監管指令所產生的成本，該指令載於同意書中。雖然本公司已實施並會持續實施節省成本的措施與效率措施，但無法保證這些行動能產生預期的財務結果。此外，本公司於 2025 年及 2024 年已減少獲利資產，並有意在未來期間開始增加獲利資產。市場條件、競爭壓力或未預見的運營挑戰等因素，可能影響本公司達成持續且可接受的未來獲利水平的能力。若本公司無法改善財務表現，可能會導致獲利水平低於可接受水平，進而對其財務狀況、資本水平與普通股價值產生不利影響。
本公司成功，且預期將持續依賴其管理團隊。本公司策略與運營將持續對管理層提出重大需求，若失去任何管理人員的服務，可能對本公司策略、運營與獲利產生不利影響。若本公司無法留住或持續招募合格員工，其策略、運營與獲利可能受到不利影響。

為成功，本公司必須識別並留住具經驗的關鍵管理人員與銷售人員，並具當地專業知識與人脈。對合格人才的競爭激烈，且具銀行知識與本公司所選地理市場經驗的合格人數有限。即使本公司識別出認為能協助其建立品牌的個體，也可能無法招募這些個體為本公司工作。此外，識別與招募具備執行本公司策略所需技能與特質的個體的過程往往耗時。本公司若無法識別、招募並留住優秀人才，將限制其追求策略目標的能力，並對其業務、財務狀況與營運成果產生重大且不利的影響。
